answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: The task was to upgrade the logging library to version 2.
quotes: The task was to upgrade the logging library to version 2.
The old version is no longer supported.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The build now takes the new version, which is the whole change; the operations team's file was not touched, and the project was not built and no tests were run.
quotes: The build now takes the new version, and that is the whole change.
I did not touch the operations team's file.
I did not build the project or run any tests.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The new version writes the time of each log line in UTC, with a letter T and a dot.
quotes: But the new version writes the time of each log line in a new form.
The new version writes the time in UTC, with a letter T and a dot.
answers.missing: How the library works apart from the form of the time it writes; the text describes only that.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: The new time form does not match the alert pattern, which expects the old form, so the operations team's alert no longer sees error lines.
quotes: So the operations team's alert on errors no longer sees our error lines.
The pattern expects the old time form: local time, a space, a comma before the milliseconds.
The new version writes the time in UTC, with a letter T and a dot.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The build and the tests were not run, the alert pattern was run only on one error line in each form, and it is not checked that the setting gives exactly the old line.
quotes: I did not build the project or run any tests.
I ran their pattern on one error line written each way.
our logs stay in local time; I have not checked that the setting gives exactly the old line

answers.question: What do I have to decide, and what does each option give and cost?
answers.answer: The text asks whether to keep the old time form with one setting in our config, or to have the operations team change its alert pattern to the new form; keeping it makes the alert fire and needs no one else to change, but leaves the local-time check unverified, while the other option moves logs to UTC but leaves errors without an alert, and the release waits, until their change is live.
quotes: You decide whether we keep the old time form on our side or the operations team changes its alert.
Keep the old time form, or ask the operations team to change the alert?
the alert keeps firing, and nobody else has to change anything
our logs stay in local time; I have not checked that the setting gives exactly the old line
logs move to UTC, which the new version intends
until their change is live, errors raise no alert, so our release waits for them
